lines.japanese: 「あのー、ところで前から思ってたんですけどー」
lines.english: “Um, by the way, there's something I've been wondering for a while.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんを送って駅に向かう途中、気になっていたことを聞いてみました。
lines.english: As I escorted Hiyoko toward the station, I decided to ask her something that had been nagging at me.

lines.japanese: 「なんでしょう？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ペンネームの細川玉木ってどこから来てるんすかね」
lines.english: “Where did your pen name, Tamaki Hosokawa, come from?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、それは本気で聞いてるんですか」
lines.english: “Wait. Are you seriously asking me that?”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんの目には、驚き半分呆れ半分がミックスされていました。
lines.english: Hiyoko's eyes held equal parts astonishment and exasperation.

lines.japanese: 「や、おおよその予想はついてるんですけど、やっぱり本人に確かめないと分からないことって、あるじゃないすか」
lines.english: “I've got a pretty good guess, but there are some things you can't know for sure until you ask the person herself, right?”

lines.japanese: 「作家とファンは深く交わらないというのが私のスタンスです。ご想像にお任せします」
lines.english: “My policy is that authors and fans should not become too deeply entangled. I'll leave it to your imagination.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、俺と日和子さんって、作家と一ファンの関係なんすか」
lines.english: “Wait. Are you and I merely an author and one of her fans?”

lines.japanese: 「はいそうです。今日付きあっていただいたのもフィールドワークの一環です」
lines.english: “Yes, we are. Your accompanying me today was part of my fieldwork.”

lines.japanese: 「これって仕事だったんすか。じゃあお給料ください」
lines.english: “This was work? Then pay me.”
“Ghk…!”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは顔を背けると、ぼそぼそと呟くように言いました。
lines.english: Hiyoko turned her face away and muttered under her breath.

lines.japanese: 「鷲介さんの想像通りです……由来はそれで合ってます……」
lines.english: “It's what you think... Your guess is correct...”

lines.japanese: 「いえあの、俺まだ何も言ってないんすけど」
lines.english: “But I haven't actually told you what my guess was.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ自由に想像していただいて結構です。鷲介さんの好きにしてください」
lines.english: “Then imagine whatever you like. Do as you please, Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、分からないし好きにしていいって言うなら、マスターかカケルくんにでも相談してみます」
lines.english: “Hmm. If I don't know and I'm free to do as I please, I suppose I'll ask the boss or Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: <10>\「やめてくださいっ」
lines.english: “Please don’t!”

lines.japanese: 「やっとこっち見てくれましたね、こんばんは！　いや、だっていま、ご自分で好きにしろと」
lines.english: “You finally looked at me! Good evening! But you did just tell me to do as I pleased.”

lines.japanese: 「はいフリファの細川君からとりました！　なにか問題ありますか！」
lines.english: “Yes! Hosokawa of the Frickies! Is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、そうですよね」
lines.english: “Well, that figures.”

lines.japanese: 分かってましたけどね。それにしたって、好きな芸能人の名前から取るって、そんな安直な。
lines.english: I had known, of course. Even so, borrowing the name of a favorite celebrity was almost painfully obvious.

lines.japanese: 生真面目な鬼教官のくせして、根はミーハーで幼稚園児なんだからこの子。ホントどこまで微笑ましいのかしら。
lines.english: For all her stern, earnest drill-sergeant ways, this girl was a starstruck kindergartner at heart. Honestly, how could anyone be this endearing?

lines.japanese: 「はあ。じゃあ下の名前はどこから？」
lines.english: “Then where did the given name come from?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「玉木っす。玉木は玉泉の玉から？」
lines.english: “Tamaki. Did you take the *tama* from Tamaizumi?”

lines.japanese: すると今度は、先ほどとは違う面持ちで黙りこくってしまいました。あれ？　タマキって可愛らしくて、別に不自然なところはない気がするけど……。
lines.english: This time she fell silent with an expression quite different from before. Huh? Tamaki was a perfectly cute name. There was nothing especially strange about it...

lines.japanese: 「せっかくだから教えてくださいよ。誰にも言いませんから」
lines.english: “Come on, tell me while we're at it. I won't tell anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「誰にも言いませんか？」
lines.english: “You won't tell anyone?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、もちろんです。ハイ、嘘ついたーら針七兆本飲ーます。はい、どうぞ」
lines.english: “Of course not. Cross my heart—if I tell, I'll swallow seven trillion needles. There. Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、もう少し現実的な数字で七本にしてください」
lines.english: “Please make that a more realistic number. Seven will do.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、このひと飲ませる気まんまんだあ」
lines.english: “Whoa! She fully intends to make me swallow them!”

lines.japanese: 「あと針だと死んでしまう可能性があるので唐辛子の実にします」
lines.english: “Also, needles might kill you, so we'll use chili peppers instead.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、どんどん現実味が増してきたあ」
lines.english: “Whoa! This is getting more realistic by the second!”

lines.japanese: 唐辛子の実を食べさせるところまでは威勢がよかったものの、いざ答えを言う段になって、日和子さんはまたしても黙りこくってしまいました。
lines.english: She had shown plenty of spirit while devising my chili-pepper punishment, but when it came time to give the answer, Hiyoko fell silent yet again.

lines.japanese: それでも俺がなにも言わずにいると、口の中でぽそぽそと小さく呟きました。
lines.english: Still, when I kept waiting in silence, she murmured so softly the words barely left her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「……タマちゃん」
lines.english: “...Tammy.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「その……友達に私のことをタマちゃんと呼ぶ子がいて、そのあだ名が気に入ってたので……」
lines.english: “One of my friends... calls me Tammy. I liked the nickname, so...”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃんと呼ばれるような名前を……」
lines.english: “I wanted a name that people could shorten to Tammy...”
“Tammy!”

lines.japanese: おおお。おおおおお。日和子さんがタマちゃん。しかも自分から。
lines.english: Ohhh. Ohhhhh. Hiyoko was Tammy. And the suggestion had come from her own lips.

lines.japanese: 「や、やめてください」
lines.english: “P-please don't.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、なんでですかあ。俺も一ファンだから呼ぶ権利ありますよねえ、タマちゃん」
lines.english: “Aw, why not? I'm a fan too, so surely I have the right to call you that. Tammy.”

lines.japanese: <10>\「やーめーてってばあ！」
lines.english: “I said stoooop!”

lines.japanese: 袖を引っ張りながら怒る日和子さんでありました。いつもと違って全然怖くないんですけど。
lines.english: Thus did Hiyoko berate me while tugging on my sleeve. Unlike usual, she wasn't frightening in the slightest.

lines.japanese: 「たまちゃん、タンマタンマ！　たまたまタマちゃんってたまらなく言いたくなっただけタマー！」
lines.english: “Tammy, time out, time out! I was suddenly seized by an untamable urge to say ‘Tammy.’ Tam-tam!”

lines.japanese: 「あたまに膿みでもたまってるんじゃないですか！　黙らないと、あたまかち割りますよ！」
lines.english: “Is something festering in that head of yours? If you don't shut up, I'll crack your skull open!”

lines.japanese: 「うひぃ、おったまげたあ！」
lines.english: “Yikes! Tammy's got a temper!”

lines.japanese: はたから見たら馬鹿ップルみたいに思われたかもしれません。あはは、楽しいーなあー。
lines.english: To anyone watching, we might have looked like a pair of lovestruck idiots. Ah ha ha. This was so much fun.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんに肩を揺さぶられながら、しかしそのとき俺は、視界の端にある人影をとらえました。
lines.english: But as Hiyoko shook me by the shoulders, I caught sight of a figure at the edge of my vision.

lines.japanese: そういえば今週の恋愛運はどうだったかしら。
lines.english: Come to think of it, what had my love horoscope said for this week?

lines.japanese: 「鷲介さん、聞いてるんですかっ！」
lines.english: “Shusuke, are you listening to me?”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてますよおー？」
lines.english: “Of course I am.”

lines.japanese: 「真面目に聞いてくださいっ！」
lines.english: “Then listen seriously!”

lines.japanese: ま、個人的な用事はあとにしましょっかね。だって楽しいんだもん、タマちゃん。
lines.english: Well, my private business could wait. Teasing Tammy was too much fun.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせしましたー」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: 俺が切符を買ってくると、彼女は太い円柱に寄りかかっていた体を起こしてうなずきました。
lines.english: When I returned with her ticket, she straightened from the thick round pillar she had been leaning against and nodded.

lines.japanese: 「いやー、今日はお付き合いいただいてありがとうございました」
lines.english: “Well, thank you for spending the day with me.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いえ、こちらこそありがとうございました」
lines.english: “Oh, no. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 深々と頭を下げる男女二人。だけど足は踏みださず。
lines.english: A man and a woman bowed deeply to each other, yet neither took a step away.

lines.japanese: かと言って切りだすような話題も見つからず。これからどこかお店へ入るには適さない時間帯です。
lines.english: Yet neither of us could find another subject to broach, and it was too late to go anywhere else.

lines.japanese: 「えーっと……」
lines.english: “Um…”

lines.japanese: 「どーでしたかね？　初デート」
lines.english: “So... how was it? Your first date?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そう……ですね、デート……ですもんね」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes... I suppose it was a date, wasn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとは楽しんでもらえました？」
lines.english: “Did you enjoy yourself, at least a little?”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは肯定も否定もせず、ただ駅コンコースの広い空間へと視線を泳がせました。
lines.english: Hiyoko neither agreed nor disagreed. Her gaze merely wandered through the vast station concourse.

lines.japanese: 「私、今日の待ちあわせ、鷲介さんが来る３０分前に着いてたんです」
lines.english: “I arrived for our meeting today thirty minutes before you did.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「ええええっ！　そんなに早く！？」
lines.english: “Whaaaat!? That early!?”

lines.japanese: だって俺が着いた時点で待ち合わせ時間の３０分前じゃん！　てことは本来の約束の一時間前！？
lines.english: After all, I had arrived thirty minutes before we were due to meet! That meant she had come a full hour before the appointed time!

lines.japanese: 俺が大げさに驚いたせいか、日和子さんはこくんとうなずいたまま俯いてしまいました。
lines.english: Perhaps I had overdone my surprise, because Hiyoko simply nodded once and lowered her head.

lines.japanese: 「す、すいません、なんか待たせてばっかりで」
lines.english: “S-sorry. I seem to have done nothing but keep you waiting today.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、いいんです。早く来たのは私の勝手ですから」
lines.english: “No, it's all right. I chose to arrive early.”

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん？」
lines.english: “Hiyoko?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はしばらく唇を噛んでいましたが、やがて思い切ったように口を開きました。
lines.english: She worried at her lip for a while, then finally opened her mouth with the air of someone taking a plunge.

lines.japanese: 「その、私……こういう風に、男のひとと約束して出かけるのは、今日が初めてだったんです」
lines.english: “The truth is... today was the first time I'd ever made plans to go out with a man like this.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、それは光栄です」
lines.english: “Well, I'm honored.”

lines.japanese: 「小さい頃から少女小説をたくさん読んできたせいで、初めてのデートっていうのに子供みたいな理想を持っちゃって……」
lines.english: “I read so many novels for girls when I was little that I developed this childish ideal of what a first date should be...”

lines.japanese: 「理想？」
lines.english: “An ideal?”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんがこくんこくんと二回うなずきました。
lines.english: Hiyoko nodded twice.

lines.japanese: 「待ちあわせのときに、男の子が私を見つけて走りよってくる、ってシチュエーションに憧れてたんです」
lines.english: “I always dreamed that when I went to meet a boy, he would spot me and come running.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんの生涯一度の大役に選ばれたのか、俺。
lines.english: She had chosen me for this once-in-a-lifetime role?

lines.japanese: そんなことに動揺してる小物の俺を、日和子さんは顔を真っ赤にしながら見上げてくれました。
lines.english: Small man that I was, the thought left me shaken. Hiyoko looked up at me, her face burning red.

lines.japanese: 「私を見つけて走ってくる鷲介さん、ちょっとかっこよかったです」
lines.english: “When you saw me and came running, Shusuke... you looked a little handsome.”

lines.japanese: 「かっこ……よかった？」
lines.english: “I looked... handsome?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ちょっと」
lines.english: “Yes. A little.”

lines.japanese: 「おかげで子供の頃からの夢が叶いました。ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Thanks to you, a dream I'd had since childhood came true. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: そこまで言うと日和子さんは、どこかぎこちないような、はにかんだ笑いをその顔に浮かべました。
lines.english: When she had said all that, Hiyoko's face softened into a shy smile that seemed almost awkward on her.

lines.japanese: 思いもよらぬ告白に俺はしばし呆然としてしまいました。
lines.english: For a moment, her unexpected confession left me dazed.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いやあはは……」
lines.english: “Oh, well, ha ha…”

lines.japanese: いや確かに俺も楽しかったし日和子さんも楽しんでくれてるなと思ってはいたけど、そこまで考えていてくれたなんて思わなかった。
lines.english: Of course I had enjoyed myself, and I had thought Hiyoko was enjoying herself too. But I had never imagined the day meant quite so much to her.

lines.japanese: いいのか俺？　こんな顔した日和子さんをこのまま帰しちゃっても。
lines.english: Was this really all right? Could I simply send Hiyoko home while she was looking at me like that?

lines.japanese: 迷った俺が視線を逸らすと、別の柱に寄りかかって抱きあっている男女が視界に入りました。
lines.english: Unable to decide, I glanced away and found a man and woman embracing against another pillar.

lines.japanese: 「ね～え、ノリくんあと５分だけ。もうちょっとここでお話しようよう」
lines.english: “Nori, pleeease. Just five more minutes. Let's stay here and talk a little longer.”

lines.japanese: 「すまない、明日も朝は早いんだ。家に帰ったらメールをするよ」
lines.english: “Forgive me. I have another early morning tomorrow. I'll email you when I get home.”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介さん？」
lines.english: “Shusuke?”

lines.japanese: 俺の視線の先を追って、ふいっと日和子さんがそのカップルを目に捉えたとき――
lines.english: Hiyoko followed my gaze. The instant her eyes found the couple—

lines.japanese: その二人は人目もはばからず、キスを交わしました。
lines.english: —they kissed without the slightest concern for who might be watching.

lines.japanese: 思わぬ光景に絶句する日和子さん。いやまあ、こんなときにあんなものを見せられたら誰だって、ねえ。
lines.english: The unexpected sight struck Hiyoko speechless. Well, anyone who saw something like that at a moment like this would be, right?

lines.japanese: 「あーっ、そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh! That reminds me.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 俺は親指と人差し指で挟んでいた紙片を唇に運びながら、ことさら軽い口調で言いました。
lines.english: I raised the scrap of paper pinched between my thumb and forefinger to my lips and spoke with studied breeziness.

lines.japanese: 「デートって言ったら定番の締めがあるじゃないすか」
lines.english: “There's a classic way to end a date, isn't there?”

lines.japanese: 「ほらほら今のご時世、こう、ね。せっかくの恋愛体験っすから、最後にお一ついかが？」
lines.english: “Come on, this is the modern age. And since you wanted the full romantic experience, how about one last thing before we part?”

lines.japanese: まあ怒られるのは承知の上で。日和子さんのことだから「ばーか」の一言であしらってくれるでしょう。それであははと笑いながらお開きー、みたいな。
lines.english: I knew perfectly well she would scold me. Hiyoko would dismiss me with a single ‘You dummy,’ we would both laugh, and that would bring the evening to a close.

lines.japanese: まあね？　お約束としてね？　いやそりゃ少しも期待してないかって言われたら嘘ですけど、まあ、八割冗談、二割本気で……あ、いや、やっぱ三割かも。
lines.english: You know—just because that's how these things go. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't hoping at all, but I was eighty percent joking and twenty percent serious... No, perhaps thirty.

lines.japanese: 思ったより心臓がばくばくいってるんで、呼吸を抑えるのに必死です。あいたたた、これ心臓痛いって。いやほんとマジ痛い。落ちつけ、落ちつけって！
lines.english: My heart was pounding far harder than I had expected, and it was all I could do to keep my breathing under control. Ow, ow, my heart actually hurt. No, seriously, it really hurt. Calm down. Calm down!

lines.japanese: あ、いや、分かった。そうか。俺シャレのふりして、マジで言ってるんだコレ。九割本気なんだ。だからこんな緊張してるんだ。
lines.english: Oh. Wait. I understood now. I was pretending this was a joke, but I meant it. I was ninety percent serious. That was why I was so nervous.
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: やたら長く感じた時間のあとに、日和子さんがゆっくりと口を開きました。ガチに取られないよう、唇へ視線をおくのは避けてたんですが……いやしかし、潤いを帯びたそちら方面についつい意識が……。
lines.english: After an interval that seemed impossibly long, Hiyoko slowly opened her mouth. I had avoided looking at her lips, lest she think I was serious... but then again, my attention kept drifting helplessly toward their soft gleam...

lines.japanese: 「あの」
lines.english: “Um…”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、ハいっ！」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha, y-yes!”

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめんなさい、まだ心の準備が……」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry. I'm not ready yet...”

lines.japanese: えっ？
lines.english: What?

lines.japanese: あ、あれ？　ええっ、うそ！？
lines.english: W-wait. What? No way!

lines.japanese: 怒られなかった！　ていうか、こここ断られなかったー！？
lines.english: She wasn't angry! More to the point, sh-sh-she hadn't said no!?

lines.japanese: 「っ！　っすよね！　いやー、ちょっと間があるんでどきどきしちゃいましたよ」
lines.english: “R-right! Of course! That pause had my heart pounding for a moment.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうですか。私もどきどきしました」
lines.english: “I-is that so? My heart was pounding too.”

lines.japanese: 「は、ハハ！　いやいや、なかなかの恋愛スキルでしたよ。これで今日一日の経験値はかなり上がったんじゃないすかね。ええもう、たぶん全体魔法とか使えますよ」
lines.english: “Ha—ha ha! Well, that was an impressive display of romantic skill. You must have gained a great deal of experience today. I bet you can cast party-wide spells now.”

lines.japanese: 「すみません、ゲームとかは分からないので」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I don't know anything about games.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、今笑いどころだったんすよ、台無しじゃないすか。ひどいなあタマちゃん」
lines.english: “Aw, that was where you were supposed to laugh. You ruined it. How cruel, Tammy.”

lines.japanese: 「あたまカチ割りますよ」
lines.english: “I'll crack your head open.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、すいません」
lines.english: “Yes. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: あははと二人の声が重なりました。うん。まあ、このくらいが、次に会うときも自然でいられるいい空気なんじゃないでしょうか。
lines.english: Our laughter mingled. Yes. This was probably the right mood to end on—one that would let us act naturally around each other the next time we met.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ここいらで」
lines.english: “Well, I should be going.”

lines.japanese: 「分かりました……また明日」
lines.english: “All right... I'll see you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、また明日。おやすみなさい」
lines.english: “Yes. Tomorrow. Good night.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんはぺこりと頭を下げて去っていきました。
lines.english: Hiyoko bowed neatly and walked away.

lines.japanese: 俺はというと、いまだ熱が冷めやらず、どうにも気持ちが落ちつきません。こういうときは、深呼吸でもして冬の空気を肺いっぱいに注ぎこんでおきましょう。
lines.english: As for me, the heat had yet to subside, and I could not settle myself at all. At times like this, the thing to do was take a deep breath and fill my lungs with winter air.

lines.japanese: すーはー、すー。すーはー、すーすー。
lines.english: In, out, in. In, out, in-in.

lines.japanese: 「さて」
lines.english: “Well, then.”

lines.japanese: 俺は大きく伸びをすると改札に背を向けて歩きはじめました。
lines.english: I stretched my arms high, turned my back on the ticket gates, and began walking.

lines.japanese: 「延長戦開始っと」
lines.english: “Time for overtime.”

lines.japanese: この時間になると、さっきまで賑やかだった通りも静かなもんです。
lines.english: By this hour, the streets that had bustled earlier were quiet.

lines.japanese: 俺はさっき日和子さんと歩いてきた道を引きかえしていました。
lines.english: I retraced the path Hiyoko and I had just taken.

lines.japanese: ある雑居ビルの前に置いてある立て看板。紫地に記号みたいなピンク文字が並んでいて、読める部分には四柱推命がうんたらかんたら。
lines.english: Outside one mixed-use building stood a signboard. Symbol-like pink letters marched across a purple background, and the parts I could read advertised something or other about Four Pillars astrology.

lines.japanese: その一番上には「柳木原の叔母　当ビル６Ｆ」と書いてあります。
lines.english: At the very top, it said, ‘The Auntie of Yanagihara—Sixth Floor.’

lines.japanese: 一階に女性用の靴屋。そしてビルの脇に「近藤ビル」と書かれたその建物は、日和子さんの担当編集である沢井さんのブログで見た写真と一致しました。
lines.english: A women's shoe store occupied the ground floor, and the name ‘Kondo Building’ was written on the side. It matched a photograph I had seen on Sawai's blog; she was Hiyoko's editor.

lines.japanese: 「なるほどねえ……」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese: さっきこの道で彼女を見かけたときは、日和子さんが一緒だったのでスルーしましたが、そうか、このビルだったのか……。
lines.english: When I had spotted her on this street earlier, Hiyoko was with me, so I had ignored her. But this was the building, then...

lines.japanese: すでに明かりの消えたそのビルは、各フロアとも閉店してるようです。
lines.english: The building was already dark, and every business inside appeared to have closed.

lines.japanese: とりあえず、彼女がここの六階の店を何度か訪れていることは、ブログの記述からして間違いないでしょう。つまり俺が沢井編集と接触するなら、ここが狙い目なのではないでしょうか。
lines.english: Judging from the blog, there could be no doubt that she had visited the establishment on the sixth floor several times. In other words, if I wanted to make contact with Sawai, this might be the place to lie in wait.
“Hmm…”

lines.japanese: 聞きこみ調査は明日にでもするとして、まずは周辺調査から始めますか。
lines.english: I could start asking questions tomorrow. For now, I would survey the area.

lines.japanese: 人目を引かないよう、ビルの周りをさりげなく一周してみました。
lines.english: Taking care not to attract attention, I made a casual circuit of the building.

lines.japanese: ビルの裏にポリバケツが固まった共同ゴミ捨て場を発見。ポリバケツのひとつに書かれた『柳木原の叔母』の文字。蓋がずれて、ゴミ袋の結び目が顔を覗かせています。
lines.english: Behind it, I found a communal garbage area with a cluster of plastic bins. One bore the words ‘The Auntie of Yanagihara.’ Its lid sat askew, with the knot of a garbage bag peeking through the gap.

lines.japanese: うーん、でもそれは人としてどうかなあ……法的にも倫理的にも抵抗あるけどなあ……。
lines.english: Hmm. But what kind of person would that make me...? The idea bothered me both legally and ethically...

lines.japanese: 「まあいいや」
lines.english: “Oh, well.”

lines.japanese: けっきょく袋の結び目を解きました。生ゴミ類が少なかったのは不幸中の幸いです。
lines.english: In the end, I untied the bag. The relative lack of food waste was one small mercy.

lines.japanese: 中からは書類のような紙片がちらほら。その中から折り込みのチラシを発見しました。なにか情報でも得られれば……。
lines.english: Inside were scattered scraps that looked like documents. Among them I found a folded advertising flyer. Perhaps it would contain something useful...

lines.japanese: 見出しは『的中率９５％！　柳木原の叔母』。
lines.english: The headline read, ‘Ninety-Five Percent Accuracy! The Auntie of Yanagihara.’

lines.japanese: 占術師紹介として、コスプレじみた衣装をまとった女性たちの顔写真がずらり並んでいます。それぞれの下には、無駄に荘厳または壮大そうなお名前。
lines.english: Under the heading ‘Meet Our Diviners’ stood a row of women in costumes bordering on cosplay. Beneath each portrait was a name of gratuitous grandeur or solemnity.

lines.japanese: うち一つが俺の注意を引きつけました。
lines.english: One of them caught my eye.

lines.japanese: 『聖龍神星＝ブルボンヌ冴子先生』
lines.english: ‘Sacred Dragon God-Star: Madame Saeko Bourbonne.’

lines.japanese: ターバンとベールで大半が隠されてはいるものの、どこかで見たような目元の女性が、どこかで見たような角度で写っておりました。
lines.english: Though a turban and veil concealed most of her face, the woman's eyes looked oddly familiar, and she had been photographed from an oddly familiar angle.

lines.japanese: 「たしか……沢井さんの下の名前も冴子とか言ったよな……？」
lines.english: “Wasn't Sawai's given name... Saeko?”

lines.japanese: さらに漁ると「１１月期シフト表」と書かれたＯＡ紙を見つけました。
lines.english: Digging further, I found a sheet of printer paper headed ‘November Shift Schedule.’

lines.japanese: ざっと目を通せば、月・金の２０時～２２時欄に「沢井」の二文字。
lines.english: A quick scan revealed the name ‘Sawai’ in the Monday and Friday slots from eight to ten in the evening.

lines.japanese: 「おまえここで働いてんのかよ！」
lines.english: “You work here!?”

lines.japanese: 思わず俺はその顔写真に目潰しを喰らわせました。
lines.english: Without thinking, I jabbed two fingers into the eyes of her photograph.

lines.japanese: 祥玄社さんの正社員である以上、こっちの仕事は副業、あくまで趣味の延長程度にやってるんでしょうけど……こんな近場で内職ですか。いい度胸してます。
lines.english: Since she was a full-time employee of Shogensha, this job must be a sideline, little more than an extension of a hobby... But moonlighting this close to the office? She had nerve.

lines.japanese: なるほど、米田さんの言ってた「沢井さんにはぜったい残業しない日がある」ってのは、こういうことだったのか。
lines.english: So this was what Yoneda had meant when she said there were certain days Sawai absolutely never worked overtime.

lines.japanese: 俺はゴミ袋の口を結びなおすと、すみやかにその場を離れました。
lines.english: I retied the garbage bag and promptly left the scene.

lines.japanese: ま、沢井編集はさておき。いまはひとまず、日和子さんとの楽しかった思い出に浸るとしましょう。
lines.english: Well, enough about Sawai. For now, I would bask in my happy memories of the day with Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: いやあ、デートって本当にいいものですね。
lines.english: Ah, dates really are wonderful things.
